capcut.role: Video editor for mobile, desktop and browser with AI tools for auto-captions, background removal, voiceover and social templates.
capcut.audience: Social creators, students and beginners who want a free, accessible editor on phone and computer.
capcut.status: Active. In the US the service is run by TikTok USDS Joint Venture LLC, per terms of use updated 15 April 2026.
pros: One editor on mobile, desktop and browser: per the help center, auto-caption detection is available on web, desktop (Windows and macOS) and mobile (iOS and Android).
Fully free version for basic editing: Standard is free and includes trimming, filters, transitions, text and music. Pro is 19.99 USD/month per an official article; price varies by region.
Refund within 14 days: per the US terms, cancelling within 14 days of starting the subscription gives a full refund, provided no paid features were used.
cons: Broad license to the company on your content: per the US terms, the user grants a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free license to use their content, and also their name and likeness, including in sponsored content.
Commercial use subject to a separate agreement: commercial use of CapCut materials is subject to the Materials License Agreement, which wasn't read.
Main AI tools are paid: per CapCut, auto-captions, motion tracking and background removal are reserved for Pro; free Standard has basic editing only.
capcut.price: Pro from 19.99 USD/month, or 179.99 USD/year, per an official article that says price varies by region and platform. Basic Standard version is free.
capcut.free: CapCut Standard is free: basic editing, filters, transitions and free effects, and a limited music library. AI tools such as auto-captions are Pro only, and there is no free storage.
plans: All paid features, including AI tools such as auto-captions, background removal and motion tracking, templates, effects and premium fonts.
All paid features, same as monthly.
Basic editing, free filters, transitions and effects, text and stickers, limited music library.
capcut.privacy: Per the US privacy policy (updated 15 April 2026), one purpose of data processing is to 'train, test, and improve technology, such as machine learning models and algorithms'. The policy doesn't say explicitly whether uploaded videos, images or voice are used for training and doesn't describe a dedicated opt-out for training.
capcut.rights: Per the US terms, CapCut doesn't own user content but receives a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free license on it, including use of the user's name and likeness in sponsored content. Commercial use of materials is subject to a separate agreement.
capcut.hebrew: Not verified: the help article on caption detection lists no languages, and an official language list wasn't read.
capcut.watch: Users report export blocked at the last step until you pay, and that features that were free moved to Pro.

veed.role: Browser video editor with auto-captions, translation and dubbing, avatars and AI tools for recording and editing.
veed.audience: Creators, marketers and teams editing in the browser who want fast captions and translation for social.
veed.status: Active. The changelog has an entry on VEED AI, an autonomous video editor, dated 19 Nov 2026, the day after the check date.
pros: Nearly unlimited captions on paid plans: all paid plans include unlimited caption generation, under a fair-use limit of 50 hours a month.
Auto-captions in Hebrew: per VEED, you can generate Hebrew auto-captions free. Downloading as SRT or VTT and translation need a paid plan.
Rights to AI images: per the AI tools terms, the user owns the AI images they create and may use them for any lawful purpose.
cons: Per-seat pricing: the price is multiplied by the number of editors in the workspace.
Points and minutes don't carry over: unused AI points and translation minutes don't roll to the next period.
Free content is used for training: per the privacy policy, content Free users upload to the site is used to train models. To object you must delete the account or upgrade.
veed.trial: Free trial for organizations only, minimum 3 users.
plans: Unlimited captions under a 50 hours/month fair-use limit, monthly or annual AI points, translation minutes by plan. Price not verified.
Plans tailored for faculty-wide use. Quote-based.
veed.privacy: Per the privacy policy (updated Nov 2026), content Free users upload to the site is used to train and develop AI models. The clause doesn't apply to content uploaded via the mobile apps. A Free user can object, but must then delete the account or upgrade to a paid plan. The clause doesn't address paid-plan content.
veed.rights: Per the AI tools terms, to the extent the law permits, the user owns the AI images and may use them for any lawful purpose, and Veed Limited won't claim ownership.
veed.hebrew: Per an official VEED tool page, you can add Hebrew auto-subtitles to video for free ('Add auto-subtitles in the Hebrew language to your video content for free'), and the tool transcribes the audio. Downloading subtitles as SRT or VTT needs a paid plan.
veed.students: The pricing page mentions 'bespoke education plans for faculty wide use' via sales. No personal student discount mentioned.

descript.role: Video and audio editor where you edit through the transcript, with AI tools for audio cleanup, captions and dubbing.
descript.audience: Podcasters, YouTubers and students editing interviews, lectures and spoken content in English or Latin-script languages.
pros: Editing through the text: the video is transcribed, and deleting or changing the transcript edits the video itself. Transcription supports 20+ languages, all in Latin script.
Discount for students and educators: the pricing page offers 'special rates' to students, teachers and non-profits via a form, without publishing the discount.
Input and outputs belong to the user: per the terms, the user owns input and output to the extent the law protects them, and Descript doesn't claim ownership.
cons: No Hebrew transcription: per the help center all supported transcription languages are in the Latin alphabet; other scripts aren't supported yet.
Limited free plan: Free has one media hour, 100 one-time AI credits and export up to 720p with a watermark.
Per-user pricing: prices are per user per month, and media-hour and AI-credit quotas are per editor.
descript.price: From 24 USD per user per month billed monthly, or 16 USD billed annually. Free plan with one media hour, 720p export and a watermark.
descript.free: Free plan: one media hour (60 minutes), 100 one-time AI credits, export up to 720p with a watermark, one user.
plans: One media hour (60 minutes), 100 one-time AI credits, export up to 720p, one user.
10 media hours and 400 AI credits/month per editor, export up to 1080p, no watermark, one user.
Same as monthly Hobbyist.
30 media hours and 800 AI credits/month per editor, export up to 4K, no watermark, 1 to 3 users.
Same as monthly Creator.
descript.privacy: Official sources contradict each other. Per the help center, production AI models don't use user data, and internal research models use only data from those who agreed to share; this can be turned off in settings ('Share data with Descript'), and is off by default on Enterprise accounts. The terms (updated 25 Feb 2025) differ.
descript.rights: Per the terms (updated 25 Feb 2025), the user owns input and output to the extent the law protects them. The user gives Descript a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free license to the content.
descript.watermark: Free plan exports carry a watermark. From Hobbyist up, exports have none.
descript.api: Yes. Per Descript's Nov 2026 blog you can search media and edit video via Underlord, MCP or the API, and the site menu includes 'API + MCP'. API docs and terms not read.
descript.hebrew: Per the help center, all supported transcription languages are in the Latin alphabet and other scripts aren't supported yet; Hebrew isn't on the list. Dubbing languages weren't checked.
descript.students: The pricing page mentions 'special rates' for students, educators and non-profits, via a form linked from the FAQ. The discount isn't published.

opusclip.role: Tool that cuts long videos into short social clips, with captions, B-roll and automatic editing of talking videos.
opusclip.audience: Content creators, podcasters and marketers who want TikTok, Reels and Shorts clips from long videos.
pros: Short clips from a long video: upload a video or paste a link and the tool makes short clips. Since OpusClip 4.0 it also auto-edits talking videos with speech cleanup, captions and B-roll.
Free plan that renews: Free includes 60 credits a month and clips up to 1080p.
Recipes and AI-assistant connection: you can save editing settings as a Recipe, and AI Producer lets you edit from ChatGPT or Claude via a plugin.
cons: No support for right-to-left languages: per the help center OpusClip doesn't support languages read right to left, including Hebrew, Arabic and Persian.
Watermark and non-commercial use on free: Free clips carry a watermark, and per the terms a commercial-use license is given only to paid-service users.
Starter is monthly billing only: Starter is 15 USD/month with 150 credits, with no annual billing.
opusclip.price: From 15 USD/month (Starter, monthly billing only), or Pro at 14.50 USD/month billed annually. Free plan with 60 credits a month and a watermark.
opusclip.free: Free plan: 60 credits a month, clips up to 1080p with a watermark.
plans: 60 credits/month, clips up to 1080p.
150 credits/month, no watermark, highest-resolution export.
300 credits/month per package, no watermark, team space with 2 seats, limited API access.
3,600 credits for 12 months, no watermark, limited API access.
opusclip.privacy: Per the terms, the user grants the company a worldwide, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to their content to provide and improve the service, monitor compliance and for legal needs. The terms don't explicitly mention model training. External AI providers may process data under their own terms. Privacy policy not read.
opusclip.rights: Per the terms, the user keeps all rights in input and output and the company doesn't claim ownership. The service is for personal, non-commercial use, but paid-service users get a commercial license.
opusclip.watermark: Free plan clips carry a watermark. From Starter up it can be removed.
opusclip.api: Yes. Per the pricing page, Pro includes 'Limited API Access' and Business includes API and custom integrations. API docs and prices not read.
opusclip.hebrew: Per the help center: "we do not support any languages that read right to left, including Hebrew". That is, no Hebrew support.

heygen.role: Platform for creating videos with talking avatars, voice cloning and video translation into other languages with lip sync.
heygen.audience: Creators, marketers and trainers who want a video with a talking character or a version of a video in another language without re-filming.
pros: Video translation with lip sync, including Hebrew: the list of languages for voice translation and lip sync includes 'Hebrew (Israel)', among 85 entries (updated 20 Aug 2026).
Free plan to try: up to 3 videos a month up to one minute, at no cost.
Personal avatar from a short recording: per HeyGen, the Avatar V model builds a consistent digital character of a person from a 15-second recording. Pro adds 4K export and professional voice cloning.
cons: Free plan is for personal use only: per the terms, free-plan outputs are allowed for personal, non-commercial and internal evaluation use only, and may not be sold or monetized.
Watermark and length limit on free: Free videos carry a watermark, up to one minute, up to 3 videos a month.

Private users' content may be used for training: per HeyGen, non-Enterprise customer data may be used to train models, with an opt-out per the privacy policy. The license in the terms also includes training models.
heygen.price: From 29 USD/month billed monthly, or 24 USD/month billed annually. Free plan with a watermark, up to 3 videos a month.
heygen.free: Free plan: up to 3 videos a month, up to one minute each, with a watermark.
plans: Up to 3 videos/month, up to one minute each.
600 credits/month, videos up to 30 minutes, export up to 1080p, up to 10 hours of narration, removes HeyGen branding.
600 credits/month, same as monthly.
1,000 credits/month, videos up to 30 minutes, export up to 4K, 16+ hours of narration, professional voice cloning.
Same as monthly Pro.
heygen.privacy: Per the trust and safety page, Enterprise customers' data isn't used for training. Other customers' data may be used to train and improve models, and you can opt out per the privacy policy. Per the terms (updated 16 Oct 2026), the license a paid-plan user gives HeyGen includes use of content 'to train or otherwise improve or modify our artificial intelligence' models.
heygen.rights: Per the terms (updated 16 Oct 2026), on Creator, Pro and Business the user owns input and outputs and HeyGen doesn't restrict commercial use. On the free plan use is limited to personal, non-commercial.
heygen.watermark: Free plan videos carry a watermark. From Creator up, HeyGen branding can be removed.
heygen.api: Yes. The pricing page links to a separate API pricing page ('Explore API pricing'), which wasn't read.
heygen.hebrew: The list of languages supported for voice translation and lip sync includes 'Hebrew (Israel)'. The article doesn't cover voice and subtitle languages, and whether subtitles display right-to-left wasn't checked.

synthesia.role: Platform for creating training and explainer videos with talking avatars from a script, including dubbing into other languages.
synthesia.audience: Training, marketing and internal-comms teams, and independent creators who need an explainer video with a presenter and no filming.
pros: Free plan with a monthly quota: Basic includes 10 video minutes and 10 dubbing minutes a month, 9 avatars and 140+ languages and voices.
Doesn't train models on customer content: per Synthesia, it doesn't use customer data, including input and output, for pre-training its AI components.

Dubbing in 70+ languages: all plans include dubbing into 70+ target languages, with a minute quota that grows with the plan. Since Synthesia 3.0 (Oct 2025) you can create a personal avatar from one photo.
cons: Watermark on the free plan: Basic videos carry a Synthesia watermark.
Small minute quota on the cheap plan: Starter adds only about 12 video minutes a month beyond the free allocation.
Promo price in the first month only: Starter is 9 USD the first month and 19 after; Pro is 49 the first month and 89 after.
synthesia.price: From 19 USD/month billed monthly (9 USD the first month in a promotion), or 14 USD/month billed annually. Free plan with 10 video minutes a month and a watermark.
synthesia.free: Free Basic plan: 500 credits a month, 10 video minutes and 10 dubbing minutes a month, 9 avatars, with a watermark.
plans: 500 credits/month, 10 video minutes/month, 10 dubbing minutes/month, 9 avatars, 140+ languages and voices.
1,250 credits/month, about 12 extra video minutes and up to 16 dubbing minutes a month beyond the free allocation, 125+ avatars, 3 personal avatars, logo removal.
15,000 credits/year, about 150 video minutes and 197 dubbing minutes a year, 125+ avatars, 3 personal avatars, logo removal.
6,000 credits/month, about 60 video minutes and up to 78 dubbing minutes a month, 180+ avatars, 5 personal avatars, logo removal.
72,000 credits/year, about 720 video minutes and 947 dubbing minutes a year, 180+ avatars, 5 personal avatars, logo removal.
synthesia.privacy: Per Synthesia's governance framework, the company doesn't use customer data, including input and output, for pre-training its AI components. Fine-tuning of components follows the customer's written instructions. Creating personal avatars and voices is subject to consent mechanisms, and content is checked at creation.
synthesia.rights: Per Synthesia, the customer keeps ownership of videos, subject to customer terms of service, which weren't read. Commercial use per plan isn't detailed on the pricing page.
synthesia.watermark: On Basic videos carry a watermark. Starter and Pro include logo removal.
synthesia.api: Yes. The pricing page links to separate API pricing information ('Explore API pricing'), which wasn't read. Which plans include API access isn't stated.
synthesia.hebrew: Per an official feature page, Synthesia produces Hebrew narration from text ('Turn any text into natural-sounding Hebrew speech in seconds'). Personal voice cloning in Hebrew needs an Enterprise plan per the page.

captions.role: App for editing talking-head videos for social, with auto-captions, avatars, voiceover and translation.
captions.audience: Creators who film themselves talking to camera and post on TikTok, Reels and Shorts.
captions.status: Active. Policy and terms documents are published under Mirage, and the European privacy policy took effect 4 Sep 2025. The date of the company rename announcement wasn't verified from a source read.
pros: Low entry price: Basic is 9.99 USD/month with 200 credits that renew, and on Android there is Lite at 4.99 USD.
No watermarks: per the help center, both the free plan and paid plans are 'No watermarks'.
Free basic captioning and editing tools: the free plan includes captions, trimming, zoom, voiceover and resizing, with one template.
cons: Free credits are one-time: the free plan has 60 to 200 credits for life, and other tools need an upgrade.
User content is used for training: per the European privacy policy, content users create is also used to train AI models, on a 'legitimate interest' basis. No dedicated opt-out is described.
Annual prices not published: the help center says only that annual billing has an automatic discount, with no amount.
captions.price: From 9.99 USD/month (Basic), and Lite on Android at 4.99 USD. Free plan with 60 to 200 one-time credits.
captions.free: Free plan with 60 to 200 credits for life, one template and basic tools (captions, trimming, zoom, voiceover, resizing).
plans: 60 to 200 credits for life, one template (Eclipse), basic tools such as captions, camera, trimming, zoom, voiceover and resizing.
200 credits that renew monthly, no watermarks.
500 credits/month, no watermarks, 2 seats (admin plus one).
1,400 credits/month, no watermarks, 3 seats.
captions.privacy: Per Mirage's privacy policy for the European Economic Area (effective 4 Sep 2025), content the user creates is used among other things 'to train our artificial intelligence/machine learning models', on a legitimate-interest basis. Special categories of data such as biometric data are used for training and AR features on a consent basis, and consent can be withdrawn.
captions.rights: Captions' website terms say input and output are 'controlled by Customer' and describe the service as for teams, businesses and organizations, not consumers. The license to the company and commercial use weren't clear.
captions.watermark: Per the help center, all plans, including the free one, are defined as no watermarks.

d-id.role: Platform for creating videos with avatars and talking characters from an image and script, in Studio and via API.
d-id.audience: Marketers, trainers and developers who need a talking character from an image, in the studio or via API.
pros: Both a studio and an API: D-ID publishes a separate price list for Studio and for the API.
Billing by video length: each video's length is rounded up to the next 15 seconds, and minutes renew every month.
V4 model on all plans: per a D-ID announcement from March 2026, V4 characters for real-time conversation with a language model are available on all plans.
cons: Watermark on Trial and Lite: Trial and Lite videos carry a D-ID watermark, and on the trial it covers the whole screen.
Minutes don't accumulate: unused minutes expire at the end of the month.
d-id.price: Per a D-ID press release of March 2026, plans start at 5.90 USD/month. Plan names and quotas not verified.
d-id.trial: A Trial plan exists whose videos carry a full-screen watermark. Trial scope not verified.
plans: Access to the V4 model, per the press release.
d-id.rights: Not verified: commercial use per plan didn't appear on the pricing page.
d-id.watermark: Trial and Lite videos carry a watermark; on the trial it covers the whole screen.
d-id.api: Yes. The pricing page links to a separate API price list, which wasn't read.

hedra.role: Platform for creating talking-character videos from an image, text and voice, with lip sync.
hedra.audience: Creators who want to animate a character or portrait so it speaks in a video, for advertising, storytelling or explanation.
pros: Talking character from a single image: the Character 3 model combines an image, text and voice into a video with lip sync and animation, up to 10 minutes long.
Commercial use on all plans: the pricing page states commercial use on all plans, from Basic at 20 USD/month with 2,000 credits.
API priced per second: Character 3 is also in the API: 2.5 cents per second at 540p, 5 cents at 720p and 6.25 cents at 1080p, paid from a dollar wallet separate from subscription credits.
cons: No free plan on the pricing page: all plans are paid, monthly billing only. After cancelling, only limited watermarked generations remain.
Monthly credits don't accumulate: credits reset each billing cycle. Only credits from separately purchased packs don't expire.

Content may be used for training in anonymized form: per the privacy policy (4 Sep 2026), Hedra may train models on aggregated or anonymized data derived also from user content. No opt-out is described.
hedra.price: From 20 USD/month for 2,000 credits, billed monthly. No free plan on the pricing page.
plans: 2,000 credits/month, slower generation, commercial use.
7,200 credits/month, faster generation, commercial use.
18,000 credits/month (up to 57,600 on higher tiers), fastest generation, commercial use, access to the Teams plan. From 100 USD/month.
hedra.privacy: Per the privacy policy (effective 4 Sep 2026), Hedra may create aggregated, de-identified or anonymized data from personal information, including user content, and use it to 'train our AI models'. The policy doesn't say explicitly that raw images, voice or videos are used for training, and describes no opt-out. A paid subscription alone doesn't guarantee content isn't used.
hedra.rights: Per the terms of use (4 Sep 2026), Hedra doesn't claim ownership of input and output, but the user grants it a broad, perpetual, irrevocable license to operate the service. The pricing page states commercial use.
hedra.watermark: After cancelling, only 'limited watermarked generations' remain. The source doesn't mention a watermark on paid plans.
hedra.api: Yes. Character 3 is in the API on Hedra's developer platform: 2.5 cents per second at 540p, 5 cents at 720p, 6.25 cents at 1080p. API calls are paid from a prepaid dollar wallet separate from subscription credits.
hedra.hebrew: Not mentioned in source: the Character 3 model page states 'full multi-language support' without a list.
